newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: CARACAS SHRS END MIXED, LITTLE CHANGED IN SLOW MKT.
newsitem.headline: CARACAS SHRS END MIXED, LITTLE CHANGED IN SLOW MKT.

text.p: Share prices on the Caracas Stock Exchange closed mixed in slow trade with foreign investors still absent from the market, brokers said.
According to preliminary figures from the exchange, the market's 19-share .IBC index edged up 0.14 percent to 9,305.16, as 20 stocks fell, 20 rose and six closed flat.
With foreign investors distracted by Wall Street movements and wary of taking positions in Venezuela due to recent labor unrest, the market has been left to local players.
"The market is very thin. In fact, the session was very slow," said Banex broker Luis Borjas.
Brokers forecast prices would drift sideways in coming sessions without the impetus of foreign capital to drive them higher.
Volume was slim with 1,037 trades for 3.591 billion bolivars ($7.3 million), the exchange said.
Among leading stocks, benchmark Electricidad de Caracas rose 2.00 bolivars to 814.00 bolivars, and telephone company CANTV rose 10.75 bolivars to 3,071.25 bolivars.

Brokers noted continued strong interest in holding company H.L. Boulton, which rose 3.00 bolivars to 55.00 bolivars, and bottling company Envases Venezolanos, which gained 2.00 bolivars to 33.50 bolivars.
The two companies, which posted impressive results recently, were expected to continue rising this week, brokers said.
